::: {.fw-banner}
**This is a fun, exploratory project** that I'm doing with my son Wyatt, who is six. We want to find out (a) which parts of football skill can be measured, and (b) how the **Soccer Factor Model** works. It comes from [Andorra & Göbel (2024), *Unveiling True Talent*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2412.05911).

The model is fitted to 593 forwards across ten seasons (2014/15–2023/24) of the Premier League, La Liga, Bundesliga, Serie A and Ligue 1. Its rankings are uncertain, and the intervals show by how much. **[How the model works →](model.qmd)**
:::

```{ojs}
//| output: false
players = FileAttachment("web/players.json").json()
draws = FileAttachment("web/draws.json").json()
curves = FileAttachment("web/curves.json").json()
skillCorr = FileAttachment("web/skill_corr.json").json()
card = FileAttachment("web/model_card.json").json()
guessFile = FileAttachment("web/wyatt_guesses.json").json()

SKILLS = ["shoot", "fox", "sniper", "create"]
KID = ({
  shoot:  {name: "Shooter",   emoji: "🚀", what: "shots"},
  fox:    {name: "Fox",       emoji: "🦊", what: "good chances"},
  sniper: {name: "Sniper",    emoji: "🎯", what: "finishing"},
  create: {name: "Playmaker", emoji: "🎁", what: "set-ups"}
})
LEAGUE = ({EPL: "Premier League", La_liga: "La Liga", Bundesliga: "Bundesliga", Serie_A: "Serie A", Ligue_1: "Ligue 1"})
COLOR_A = "#2a78d6"
COLOR_B = "#eb6834"

ownLift = new Map(players.map(p => [p.i, mean(draws.goals90_actual[p.i]) - mean(draws.goals90_level[p.i])]))
ownLiftStars = { const v = [...ownLift.values()].sort((a, b) => a - b); return new Map([...ownLift].map(([i, x]) => [i, Math.min(5, Math.max(1, Math.ceil(5 * (v.indexOf(x) + 0.5) / v.length)))])); }
nSeasons = new Map(players.map(p => [p.i, new Set(p.seasons.filter(s => s.minutes >= 270).map(s => s.season)).size]))
bySAR = [...players].sort((a, b) => b.SAR.mean - a.SAR.mean)
byName = new Map(players.map(p => [p.name, p]))
names = players.map(p => p.name).sort((a, b) => a.localeCompare(b))
norm = s => s.toLowerCase().normalize("NFD").replace(/[̀-ͯ]/g, "")

function findPlayer(q, fallback) {
  if (q && byName.has(q)) return byName.get(q);
  if (q && q.trim().length >= 2) {
    const n = norm(q.trim());
    const hit = bySAR.find(p => norm(p.name).includes(n));
    if (hit) return hit;
  }
  return byName.get(fallback);
}
function picker(label, value) {
  return Inputs.text({label, value, datalist: names, placeholder: "Type a player's name…", autocomplete: "off", spellcheck: false});
}
function starsHTML(n) {
  return html`<span class="fw-stars" aria-label="${n} out of 5 stars">${"★".repeat(n)}<span class="off">${"★".repeat(5 - n)}</span></span>`;
}
function initials(name) {
  const parts = name.split(/\s+/).filter(Boolean);
  return (parts.length === 1 ? parts[0].slice(0, 2) : parts[0][0] + parts[parts.length - 1][0]).toUpperCase();
}
q = (arr, p) => { const s = [...arr].sort((a, b) => a - b); const h = (s.length - 1) * p, lo = Math.floor(h); return s[lo] + (s[Math.min(lo + 1, s.length - 1)] - s[lo]) * (h - lo); }
mean = arr => arr.reduce((a, b) => a + b, 0) / arr.length
function poisson(lambda) {   // Knuth; fine for the small rates here
  const L = Math.exp(-lambda); let k = 0, p = 1;
  do { k++; p *= Math.random(); } while (p > L);
  return k - 1;
}
function skillSays(k, p) {
  const m = Math.exp(p.skills[k].mean), st = p.skills[k].stars;
  if (k === "shoot")  return m >= 1.05 ? `On an average team, he'd take ${m.toFixed(1)}× as many shots as a typical forward.` : m <= 0.95 ? `On an average team, he'd take fewer shots than a typical forward (${m.toFixed(1)}×).` : "On an average team, he'd take about as many shots as a typical forward.";
  if (k === "fox")    return m >= 1.05 ? `He finds better spots: on an average team his chances would be ${m.toFixed(1)}× as good as a typical forward's.` : m <= 0.95 ? `He shoots from harder places than a typical forward (${m.toFixed(1)}×).` : "His chances are about as good as a typical forward's.";
  if (k === "sniper") return st >= 4 ? "Scores a bit more often than his chances say he should." : st <= 2 ? "Scores a little less often than his chances say, even counting his teams." : "Scores about as often as his chances say. Most forwards do.";
  if (k === "create") return m >= 1.05 ? `Sets up ${m.toFixed(1)}× as many shots for team-mates as a typical forward.` : m <= 0.95 ? `Sets up fewer shots for team-mates than a typical forward (${m.toFixed(1)}×).` : "Sets up about as many shots as a typical forward.";
}
```

### 1. Pick a player

Type a name. Each player gets **stars** for four football skills. The stars compare him with the other 592 forwards.

```{ojs}
viewof cardName = picker("Player", "Erling Haaland")
```

```{ojs}
cardPlayer = findPlayer(cardName, "Erling Haaland")
{
  const p = cardPlayer;
  const seasons = p.first_season === p.last_season ? `${p.first_season}/${(p.first_season + 1) % 100}` : `${p.first_season}/${String((p.first_season + 1) % 100).padStart(2, "0")}–${p.last_season}/${String((p.last_season + 1) % 100).padStart(2, "0")}`;
  const per10 = (p.goals90_level.mean * 10).toFixed(1);
  return html`<div class="fw-card">
    <div class="fw-card-head">
      <div class="fw-badge" aria-hidden="true">${initials(p.name)}</div>
      <div>
        <div class="fw-card-name">${p.name}${p.pool_reason === "wyatt_pick" ? html`<span class="fw-pick-tag">Wyatt's pick</span>` : ""}</div>
        <div class="fw-card-sub">${p.teams.join(" · ")}<br>${p.leagues.map(l => LEAGUE[l]).join(", ")} · ${seasons} · ${p.games} games</div>
      </div>
    </div>
    ${SKILLS.map(k => html`<div class="fw-skill-row">
      <div class="fw-skill-emoji" aria-hidden="true">${KID[k].emoji}</div>
      <div class="fw-skill-name">${KID[k].name}</div>
      ${starsHTML(p.skills[k].stars)}
      <div class="fw-skill-says">${skillSays(k, p)}</div>
    </div>`)}
    <div class="fw-skill-row">
      <div class="fw-skill-emoji" aria-hidden="true">⚽</div>
      <div class="fw-skill-name">Goal power</div>
      ${starsHTML(p.SAR.stars)}
      <div class="fw-skill-says">If every team were equally good, he'd score about <b>${per10} goals every 10 full games</b> (not counting penalties).</div>
    </div>
  </div>`;
}
```

### 2. Who's better? Play 100 pretend matches

Pick two players. The computer plays **100 pretend matches**, with both players in equally good teams. Each dot is one match: a blue dot means the first player scored more, an orange dot means the second player did, and a grey dot means a tie.

```{ojs}
viewof raceAName = picker("Blue player", "Lionel Messi")
viewof raceBName = picker("Orange player", "Cristiano Ronaldo")
viewof play = Inputs.button("⚽ Play 100 matches!")
```

```{ojs}
raceA = findPlayer(raceAName, "Lionel Messi")
raceB = findPlayer(raceBName, "Cristiano Ronaldo")
race = {
  const A = raceA, B = raceB;
  const la = draws.goals90_level[A.i], lb = draws.goals90_level[B.i];
  const render = (res, done) => {
    const nA = res.filter(r => r === "a").length, nB = res.filter(r => r === "b").length, nT = res.filter(r => r === "t").length;
    const dots = Array.from({length: 100}, (_, k) => html`<div class="fw-dot ${res[k] ?? ""}"></div>`);
    let verdict = "";
    if (done) {
      verdict = Math.abs(nA - nB) < 10 ? "Too close to call! Press again and it might come out the other way." : `${nA > nB ? A.name : B.name} scored more in more matches.`;
      if (nT > 60) verdict += " Lots of ties: scoring goals is hard, even for great players!";
    }
    return html`<div class="fw-race">
      <div class="fw-dots" role="img" aria-label="${nA} blue, ${nB} orange, ${nT} ties">${dots}</div>
      <div class="fw-tally">
        <div class="fw-tally-row"><span class="fw-key" style="background:${COLOR_A}"></span><b>${nA}</b> ${A.name} scored more</div>
        <div class="fw-tally-row"><span class="fw-key" style="background:${COLOR_B}"></span><b>${nB}</b> ${B.name} scored more</div>
        <div class="fw-tally-row"><span class="fw-key" style="background:var(--fw-tie)"></span><b>${nT}</b> ties</div>
        <p style="margin-top:0.8rem">${done ? verdict : play === 0 ? "Press the button to play!" : "Playing…"}</p>
      </div>
    </div>`;
  };
  if (play === 0) { yield render([], false); return; }
  const res = [];
  for (let m = 0; m < 100; m++) {
    const j = Math.floor(Math.random() * la.length);   // a random posterior draw for each match
    const ga = poisson(la[j]), gb = poisson(lb[j]);
    res.push(ga > gb ? "a" : gb > ga ? "b" : "t");
  }
  for (let k = 0; k <= 100; k += 2) {
    yield render(res.slice(0, k), k === 100);
    await Promises.delay(45);
  }
}
```

::: {.fw-section-note}
Why are the results different every time you press the button? Because football is full of luck, and because the model isn't 100% sure exactly how good each player is.
:::

### 3. Is the team helping?

Good players on great teams get more chances. The model works out how many goals a player would score **on an average team**, and how many it expects **with his real teams**.

```{ojs}
viewof teamName = picker("Player", "Robert Lewandowski")
```

```{ojs}
{
  const p = findPlayer(teamName, "Robert Lewandowski");
  const lvl = mean(draws.goals90_level[p.i]) * 10, act = mean(draws.goals90_actual[p.i]) * 10;
  const balls = (x, ghost) => {
    const full = Math.floor(x), part = x - full >= 0.5 ? 1 : 0;
    return html`<span class="fw-balls">${"⚽".repeat(full)}${part ? html`<span class="ghost">⚽</span>` : ""}</span>`;
  };
  const diff = act - lvl;
  const msg = diff > 0.2 ? `His teams helped him: about ${diff.toFixed(1)} extra goals every 10 full games.`
            : diff < -0.2 ? `His teams made it harder: on an average team he'd score about ${(-diff).toFixed(1)} more goals every 10 full games.`
            : "His teams didn't change much: what you see is mostly him.";
  return html`<div>
    <div class="fw-team-row"><div class="fw-team-label">On an average team: ${lvl.toFixed(1)} goals every 10 full games</div>${balls(lvl)}</div>
    <div class="fw-team-row"><div class="fw-team-label">With his real teams (${p.teams.slice(0, 3).join(", ")}${p.teams.length > 3 ? "…" : ""}): ${act.toFixed(1)} goals every 10 full games</div>${balls(act)}</div>
    <p><b>${msg}</b></p>
  </div>`;
}
```

### 4. When are forwards at their best?

The line shows the usual pattern of goal scoring across a forward's seasons, for all 593 players. The thin lines are other possible answers the model thinks could be true.

```{ojs}
viewof careerName = picker("Show a player's seasons", "Harry Kane")
```

```{ojs}
careerData = {
  const nd = curves.shoot.draws.length;
  const rows = [];
  for (let d = 0; d < nd; d++) curves.season_index.forEach((s, t) => rows.push({draw: d, season: s,
    goals: Math.exp(curves.shoot.draws[d][t] + curves.fox.draws[d][t] + curves.sniper.draws[d][t])}));
  const meanLine = curves.season_index.map((s, t) => ({season: s,
    goals: Math.exp(curves.shoot.mean[t] + curves.fox.mean[t] + curves.sniper.mean[t])}));
  return {rows, meanLine};
}
{
  const p = findPlayer(careerName, "Harry Kane");
  const idx = [...new Set(p.seasons.filter(s => s.minutes >= 270).map(s => s.season_index))];
  const marks = careerData.meanLine.filter(r => idx.includes(r.season));
  return Plot.plot({
    width: Math.min(width, 720), height: 300, marginLeft: 56,
    x: {label: "Season in our data →", ticks: 10, tickFormat: d => `${d}`},
    y: {label: "↑ Goals compared with average", tickFormat: d => `${Math.round((d - 1) * 100)}%`, grid: true},
    marks: [
      Plot.ruleY([1], {stroke: "#8a8983"}),
      Plot.line(careerData.rows, {x: "season", y: "goals", z: "draw", stroke: "#2a78d6", strokeOpacity: 0.15, strokeWidth: 1}),
      Plot.line(careerData.meanLine, {x: "season", y: "goals", stroke: "#2a78d6", strokeWidth: 3}),
      Plot.dot(marks, {x: "season", y: "goals", r: 8, fill: "#eb6834", stroke: "white", strokeWidth: 2}),
      Plot.text(marks.slice(-1), {x: "season", y: "goals", text: () => p.name, dy: -16, fontWeight: 700, fill: "#0b0b0b"}),
      Plot.tip(careerData.meanLine, Plot.pointerX({x: "season", y: "goals", title: d => `Season ${d.season}: ${d.goals >= 1 ? "+" : ""}${Math.round((d.goals - 1) * 100)}% goals`}))
    ]
  });
}
```

::: {.fw-section-note}
Forwards tend to score a little more in their first few seasons in our data, then slowly a bit less. The change is small, only a few percent. "Season 1" means a player's first season in our data, which starts in 2014, so for older players like Messi it isn't really their first season.
:::

### 5. The question jar

Pick a question, and the model answers with its top 10.

```{ojs}
QUESTIONS = [
  {q: "Who's the best goal scorer?", key: p => p.SAR.mean, say: p => `${(p.goals90_level.mean * 10).toFixed(1)} goals every 10 full games on an average team`, stars: p => p.SAR.stars},
  {q: "Who shoots the most?", key: p => p.skills.shoot.mean, say: p => `${Math.exp(p.skills.shoot.mean).toFixed(1)}× a typical forward's shots`, stars: p => p.skills.shoot.stars},
  {q: "Who finds the best chances?", key: p => p.skills.fox.mean, say: p => `chances ${Math.exp(p.skills.fox.mean).toFixed(1)}× as good as typical`, stars: p => p.skills.fox.stars},
  {q: "Who's the best finisher?", key: p => p.skills.sniper.mean, say: p => `scores ${Math.round((Math.exp(p.skills.sniper.mean) - 1) * 100)}% more than his chances say`, stars: p => p.skills.sniper.stars},
  {q: "Who sets up the most shots?", key: p => p.skills.create.mean, say: p => `${Math.exp(p.skills.create.mean).toFixed(1)}× a typical forward's set-ups`, stars: p => p.skills.create.stars},
  {q: "Whose team helped him most?", key: p => ownLift.get(p.i), say: p => `+${(ownLift.get(p.i) * 10).toFixed(1)} goals every 10 full games from his teams`, stars: p => ownLiftStars.get(p.i)}
]
viewof question = Inputs.radio(QUESTIONS, {format: d => d.q, value: QUESTIONS[0]})
viewof jarEstablished = Inputs.toggle({label: "Only players with 3 or more seasons", value: true})
```

```{ojs}
{
  const top = players.filter(p => !jarEstablished || nSeasons.get(p.i) >= 3)
    .sort((a, b) => question.key(b) - question.key(a)).slice(0, 10);
  const medal = i => ["🥇", "🥈", "🥉"][i] ?? `${i + 1}`;
  return html`<ol class="fw-ladder">${top.map((p, i) => html`<li>
    <span class="fw-rank">${medal(i)}</span>
    <span><span class="who">${p.name}</span>${p.pool_reason === "wyatt_pick" ? html`<span class="fw-pick-tag">Wyatt's pick</span>` : ""}<br><span class="what">${question.say(p)}</span></span>
    ${starsHTML(question.stars(p))}
  </li>`)}</ol>`;
}
```

### 6. Wyatt's guesses vs the model

Before looking at the model, choose up to five players and put them in order, from the best goal scorer (1) down. Then see what the model thinks.

```{ojs}
defaultGuesses = (guessFile.players ?? []).concat(["", "", "", "", ""]).slice(0, 5)
viewof guesses = Inputs.form(defaultGuesses.map((g, i) => picker(`${i + 1}.`, g)))
viewof reveal = Inputs.toggle({label: "Show what the model thinks", value: false})
```

```{ojs}
{
  const chosen = guesses.map(g => g && g.trim() ? findPlayer(g, null) : null).filter(Boolean);
  const unique = chosen.filter((p, i) => chosen.findIndex(c => c.i === p.i) === i);
  if (unique.length < 2) return html`<p class="fw-section-note">Type at least two players to compare.</p>`;
  if (!reveal) return html`<p class="fw-section-note">${unique.length} players chosen. Switch on "Show what the model thinks" when you're ready!</p>`;
  const nd = draws.n_draws;
  const best = unique.map(() => 0);
  for (let d = 0; d < nd; d++) {
    let bi = 0;
    unique.forEach((p, k) => { if (draws.goals90_level[p.i][d] > draws.goals90_level[unique[bi].i][d]) bi = k; });
    best[bi]++;
  }
  const modelOrder = [...unique].sort((a, b) => b.SAR.mean - a.SAR.mean);
  return html`<table class="fw-guess-table">
    <thead><tr><th>Player</th><th class="num">Wyatt's rank</th><th class="num">Model's rank</th><th class="num">Chance he's the best of these</th></tr></thead>
    <tbody>${unique.map((p, k) => html`<tr>
      <td>${p.name}</td><td class="num">${k + 1}</td><td class="num">${modelOrder.indexOf(p) + 1}${modelOrder.indexOf(p) === k ? " ✅" : ""}</td>
      <td class="num">${Math.round(100 * best[k] / nd)}%</td></tr>`)}</tbody>
  </table>
  <p class="fw-section-note">The last column shows how sure the model is. The model keeps track of how sure it is. Here it often isn't very sure.</p>`;
}
```

:::

## 📊 Grown-up mode

### What is being estimated

Each forward $p$ has four correlated effects, $\alpha_p = (\alpha^{\text{shoot}}, \alpha^{\text{fox}}, \alpha^{\text{sniper}}, \alpha^{\text{create}}) \sim \text{MVN}(0, \Sigma)$, with an LKJ prior on the correlations. For each player-season $r$, every skill $k$ gets its own linear predictor:

$$\eta_{k,r} = \mu_k + \lambda_{k,\text{league}(r)} + \beta_k\,\text{TS}_r + \gamma_k\,\overline{\text{TS}}_{p(r)} + h_k(N^S_r) + \alpha_{p(r),k}$$

TS is the paper's team factor, measured before kickoff: the team's points-per-game gap to each opponent, averaged over its season. $\overline{\text{TS}}_p$ is the player's average TS across his seasons, a Mundlak term. Better forwards tend to play for better teams, and this term absorbs that link, so $\beta_k$ measures the effect of a stronger team on the same player. A player's skill is $\theta_{p,k} = \alpha_{p,k} + \gamma_k \overline{\text{TS}}_p$. $h_k$ is a Matérn-5/2 HSGP maturity curve over seasons observed. The likelihoods are:

| Skill | Data | Likelihood |
|---|---|---|
| Shooting | non-penalty shots | NegBin$(\tfrac{\text{min}}{90} e^{\eta_\text{shoot}})$ |
| Fox | npxG per shot | $\log(\text{npxG}/\text{shot}) \sim N(\eta_\text{fox}, \sigma/\sqrt{\text{shots}})$ |
| Sniper | each non-penalty shot | Bernoulli$(\text{logit}^{-1}(\text{logit}\,\text{xG}_i + \eta_\text{sniper}))$, fitted through a second-order approximation |
| Creating | key passes | NegBin$(\tfrac{\text{min}}{90} e^{\eta_\text{create}})$ |

Shots/90 × xG/shot × goals/xG = goals/90, so the first three skills multiply into expected non-penalty goals per 90. SAR is that rate with the team factor set to zero (a level field), minus the replacement pool's rate. PAR keeps each player's real team strength. PAR − SAR is his team lift relative to the pool's. All intervals are 83%, as in the paper.

### Ranking ladder

```{ojs}
DIMS = [
  {key: "SAR", label: "SAR: goals/90 above replacement (level field)", neutral: 0, fmt: d3.format("+.2f")},
  {key: "team_lift", label: "PAR − SAR: team lift relative to the replacement pool (goals/90)", neutral: 0, fmt: d3.format("+.2f")},
  {key: "shoot", label: "Shooting: shots/90 multiplier", neutral: 1, fmt: d => `${d.toFixed(2)}×`},
  {key: "fox", label: "Fox: xG/shot multiplier", neutral: 1, fmt: d => `${d.toFixed(2)}×`},
  {key: "sniper", label: "Sniper: goals/xG multiplier", neutral: 1, fmt: d => `${d.toFixed(2)}×`},
  {key: "create", label: "Creating: key passes/90 multiplier", neutral: 1, fmt: d => `${d.toFixed(2)}×`}
]
POOLS = [
  {label: "Middle 20% of forwards (40th–60th percentile), the default", lo: 0.4, hi: 0.6},
  {label: "Middle half (25th–75th percentile)", lo: 0.25, hi: 0.75},
  {label: "Bottom half (0–50th percentile)", lo: 0, hi: 0.5},
  {label: "Everyone (the pool average)", lo: 0, hi: 1}
]
viewof pool = Inputs.select(POOLS, {label: "Replacement pool", format: d => d.label})
```

```{ojs}
//| output: false
rlp = {
  const m = players.map(p => p.goals90_level.mean), s = [...m].sort((a, b) => a - b);
  const lo = q(s, pool.lo), hi = q(s, pool.hi);
  const inPool = players.filter((p, i) => m[i] >= lo && m[i] <= hi).map(p => p.i);
  const nd = draws.n_draws;
  const lvl = Array.from({length: nd}, (_, d) => mean(inPool.map(i => draws.goals90_level[i][d])));
  const act = Array.from({length: nd}, (_, d) => mean(inPool.map(i => draws.goals90_actual[i][d])));
  return {n: inPool.length, lvl, act};
}
function dimDraws(key, i) {
  if (key === "SAR") return draws.goals90_level[i].map((v, d) => v - rlp.lvl[d]);
  if (key === "team_lift") return draws.goals90_actual[i].map((v, d) => (v - rlp.act[d]) - (draws.goals90_level[i][d] - rlp.lvl[d]));
  return draws.skill[key][i].map(Math.exp);
}
summaries = new Map(DIMS.map(dim => [dim.key, players.map(p => {
  const x = dimDraws(dim.key, p.i);
  return {i: p.i, name: p.name, mean: mean(x), lo: q(x, 0.085), hi: q(x, 0.915), leagues: p.leagues, minutes: p.minutes, seasons: nSeasons.get(p.i)};
})]))
```

```{ojs}
viewof ladderDim = Inputs.select(DIMS, {label: "Rank by", format: d => d.label})
viewof ladderLeagues = Inputs.checkbox(Object.keys(LEAGUE), {label: "Leagues", format: d => LEAGUE[d], value: Object.keys(LEAGUE)})
viewof ladderMin = Inputs.range([2500, 20000], {label: "Min. minutes", step: 500, value: 6000})
viewof ladderSeasons = Inputs.range([1, 10], {label: "Min. seasons", step: 1, value: 1})
viewof ladderSort = Inputs.radio(["Posterior mean", "Lower end of the 83% interval (surest first)"], {label: "Order by", value: "Posterior mean"})
viewof ladderN = Inputs.range([10, 60], {label: "Show top", step: 5, value: 25})
```

```{ojs}
{
  const rows = summaries.get(ladderDim.key)
    .filter(r => r.minutes >= ladderMin && r.seasons >= ladderSeasons && r.leagues.some(l => ladderLeagues.includes(l)))
    .sort(ladderSort.startsWith("Lower") ? (a, b) => b.lo - a.lo : (a, b) => b.mean - a.mean).slice(0, ladderN);
  return Plot.plot({
    width: Math.min(width, 860), height: 40 + rows.length * 20, marginLeft: 170,
    x: {label: ladderDim.label + " →", grid: true, tickFormat: ladderDim.fmt},
    y: {domain: rows.map(r => r.name), label: null},
    marks: [
      Plot.ruleX([ladderDim.neutral], {stroke: "#8a8983", strokeDasharray: "3,3"}),
      Plot.ruleY(rows, {y: "name", x1: "lo", x2: "hi", stroke: COLOR_A, strokeWidth: 2, strokeOpacity: 0.55}),
      Plot.dot(rows, {y: "name", x: "mean", r: 4.5, fill: COLOR_A, stroke: "white", strokeWidth: 1.5}),
      Plot.tip(rows, Plot.pointerY({y: "name", x: "mean",
        title: r => `${r.name}\n${ladderDim.fmt(r.mean)}  (83%: ${ladderDim.fmt(r.lo)} to ${ladderDim.fmt(r.hi)})\n${r.minutes.toLocaleString()} minutes, ${r.seasons} season${r.seasons === 1 ? "" : "s"}`}))
    ]
  });
}
```

```{ojs}
md`<span class="fw-section-note">Dots are posterior means and bars are 83% intervals. SAR and team lift are measured against a replacement pool of ${rlp.n} players. Changing the pool moves every SAR value by the same amount in each draw, so the ranking stays the same but the zero line moves. Each player has one skill, averaged over his seasons in the window. A two-season player is measured over those two seasons alone, while a nine-season veteran's estimate includes his late-career decline. "Min. seasons" restricts the ladder to established players, and "surest first" ranks players by how high the model is confident they reach.</span>`
```

### Cross-cutting two skills

```{ojs}
viewof xDim = Inputs.select(DIMS, {label: "x", format: d => d.label, value: DIMS[2]})
viewof yDim = Inputs.select(DIMS, {label: "y", format: d => d.label, value: DIMS[3]})
viewof highlightText = Inputs.text({label: "Highlight", placeholder: "Comma-separated names, e.g. Messi, Haaland, Kane", value: "Messi, Haaland, Kane, Mbappé, Salah"})
```

```{ojs}
{
  const xs = summaries.get(xDim.key), ys = summaries.get(yDim.key);
  const rows = players.map(p => ({name: p.name, x: xs[p.i].mean, xlo: xs[p.i].lo, xhi: xs[p.i].hi, y: ys[p.i].mean, ylo: ys[p.i].lo, yhi: ys[p.i].hi, minutes: p.minutes}));
  const wanted = highlightText.split(",").map(s => s.trim()).filter(s => s.length >= 2).map(s => findPlayer(s, null)).filter(Boolean).map(p => p.name);
  const hi = rows.filter(r => wanted.includes(r.name));
  return Plot.plot({
    width: Math.min(width, 860), height: 520, marginLeft: 60, marginBottom: 44,
    x: {label: xDim.label + " →", tickFormat: xDim.fmt, grid: true},
    y: {label: "↑ " + yDim.label, tickFormat: yDim.fmt, grid: true},
    marks: [
      Plot.ruleX([xDim.neutral], {stroke: "#8a8983", strokeDasharray: "3,3"}),
      Plot.ruleY([yDim.neutral], {stroke: "#8a8983", strokeDasharray: "3,3"}),
      Plot.dot(rows, {x: "x", y: "y", r: 2.8, fill: "#9b9a94", fillOpacity: 0.55}),
      Plot.ruleY(hi, {y: "y", x1: "xlo", x2: "xhi", stroke: COLOR_B, strokeWidth: 2}),
      Plot.ruleX(hi, {x: "x", y1: "ylo", y2: "yhi", stroke: COLOR_B, strokeWidth: 2}),
      Plot.dot(hi, {x: "x", y: "y", r: 5.5, fill: COLOR_B, stroke: "white", strokeWidth: 2}),
      Plot.text(hi, {x: "x", y: "y", text: "name", dx: 9, dy: -9, textAnchor: "start", fontWeight: 600, fill: "#0b0b0b", stroke: "white", strokeWidth: 3, paintOrder: "stroke"}),
      Plot.tip(rows, Plot.pointer({x: "x", y: "y", title: r => `${r.name}\nx: ${xDim.fmt(r.x)}\ny: ${yDim.fmt(r.y)}\n${r.minutes.toLocaleString()} minutes`}))
    ]
  });
}
```

::: {.fw-section-note}
Grey dots are posterior means for all 593 forwards. Highlighted players also show their 83% intervals in both directions. The dashed lines mark a typical forward (×1) or the replacement level (0).
:::

### Head to head

```{ojs}
viewof h2hAName = picker("Player A", "Lionel Messi")
viewof h2hBName = picker("Player B", "Cristiano Ronaldo")
```

```{ojs}
{
  const A = findPlayer(h2hAName, "Lionel Messi"), B = findPlayer(h2hBName, "Cristiano Ronaldo");
  const rows = DIMS.map(dim => {
    const a = dimDraws(dim.key, A.i), b = dimDraws(dim.key, B.i);
    const pA = mean(a.map((v, d) => v > b[d] ? 1 : 0));
    return {dim, a: mean(a), b: mean(b), pA};
  });
  const diff = draws.goals90_level[A.i].map((v, d) => v - draws.goals90_level[B.i][d]);
  const pDiff = mean(diff.map(v => v > 0 ? 1 : 0));
  const table = html`<table class="fw-prob-table">
    <thead><tr><th>Dimension</th><th style="color:${COLOR_A}">${A.name}</th><th style="color:${COLOR_B}">${B.name}</th><th>P(A higher)</th></tr></thead>
    <tbody>${rows.map(r => html`<tr><td>${r.dim.label}</td><td class="num">${r.dim.fmt(r.a)}</td><td class="num">${r.dim.fmt(r.b)}</td><td class="num"><b>${Math.round(r.pA * 100)}%</b></td></tr>`)}</tbody>
  </table>`;
  const chart = Plot.plot({
    width: Math.min(width, 720), height: 220, marginLeft: 50,
    x: {label: `Level-field goals/90: ${A.name} minus ${B.name} →`, tickFormat: "+.2f"},
    y: {label: "↑ Posterior draws", grid: true},
    marks: [
      Plot.rectY(diff, Plot.binX({y: "count"}, {x: d => d, fill: d => d > 0 ? COLOR_A : COLOR_B, thresholds: 30, inset: 1})),
      Plot.ruleX([0], {stroke: "#0b0b0b"}),
      Plot.ruleY([0])
    ]
  });
  return html`${table}<p style="margin-top:1rem">The posterior says <b>${A.name}</b> is the more skilled scorer, on a level field, with probability <b>${Math.round(pDiff * 100)}%</b>.</p>${chart}`;
}
```

### How the skills go together

```{ojs}
{
  const lab = k => KID[k].name;
  const cells = [];
  skillCorr.skills.forEach((r, i) => skillCorr.skills.forEach((c, j) => cells.push({
    row: lab(r), col: lab(c), v: skillCorr.mean[i][j], lo: skillCorr.lo83[i][j], hi: skillCorr.hi83[i][j], diag: i === j})));
  const order = skillCorr.skills.map(lab);
  return Plot.plot({
    width: Math.min(width, 520), height: 380, marginLeft: 90, marginBottom: 40, padding: 0.04,
    x: {domain: order, label: null, axis: "top"}, y: {domain: order, label: null},
    color: {type: "linear", domain: [-1, 0, 1], range: [COLOR_B, "#f1f0ee", COLOR_A], legend: true, label: "Correlation"},
    marks: [
      Plot.cell(cells, {x: "col", y: "row", fill: d => d.diag ? null : d.v, stroke: "#e4e3df", rx: 4}),
      Plot.text(cells.filter(d => !d.diag), {x: "col", y: "row", text: d => `${d.v.toFixed(2)}\n[${d.lo.toFixed(2)}, ${d.hi.toFixed(2)}]`, fill: "#0b0b0b", fontSize: 11, lineHeight: 1.2}),
      Plot.tip(cells.filter(d => !d.diag), Plot.pointer({x: "col", y: "row", title: d => `${d.row} × ${d.col}\n${d.v.toFixed(2)} (83%: ${d.lo.toFixed(2)} to ${d.hi.toFixed(2)})`}))
    ]
  });
}
```

::: {.fw-section-note}
These are posterior correlations between the skills, with 83% intervals; an LKJ distribution is their prior. The most precisely estimated pattern is that players who get very good chances tend to create less. Finishing varies about half as much as the other skills and is the hardest to estimate for any one player, so Sniper stars only move away from 3 when the 83% interval excludes zero.
:::

### Maturity curves

```{ojs}
{
  const rows = [];
  SKILLS.forEach(k => curves.season_index.forEach((s, t) => rows.push({skill: `${KID[k].emoji} ${KID[k].name}`, season: s,
    m: Math.exp(curves[k].mean[t]), lo: Math.exp(curves[k].lo83[t]), hi: Math.exp(curves[k].hi83[t])})));
  return Plot.plot({
    width: Math.min(width, 860), height: 260, marginLeft: 50,
    fx: {label: null}, x: {label: "Seasons observed →", ticks: 5},
    y: {label: "↑ Multiplier", tickFormat: d => `${d.toFixed(2)}×`, grid: true},
    marks: [
      Plot.ruleY([1], {stroke: "#8a8983"}),
      Plot.areaY(rows, {fx: "skill", x: "season", y1: "lo", y2: "hi", fill: COLOR_A, fillOpacity: 0.18}),
      Plot.line(rows, {fx: "skill", x: "season", y: "m", stroke: COLOR_A, strokeWidth: 2}),
      Plot.tip(rows, Plot.pointerX({fx: "skill", x: "season", y: "m", title: d => `${d.skill}, season ${d.season}: ${d.m.toFixed(3)}× (83%: ${d.lo.toFixed(3)}–${d.hi.toFixed(3)})`}))
    ]
  });
}
```

::: {.fw-section-note}
Population HSGP curves, with the multiplier shown relative to the average player-season. Across their seasons in the window, forwards shoot a little less but take better chances. "Seasons observed" counts from 2014/15, so it is left-censored for veterans.
:::
